summary: Demo/walkthrough of Redwood Console focusing on tracing, error analysis, and request-logs for Atlas Health's inference workloads. Showed end-to-end request trace, how to pivot from an error example to root cause, filtering and redaction controls in request logs, and suggested next steps for a POC and security review.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Jamie (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we have about 45 minutes, sounds like Atlass Health — sorry Atlas Health? — team is short on time so we'll focus on the console flows. Um quick intros - I'm Jamie, AE.
[00:00:12] Priya (Atlas - CTO): Hi, Priya here, Marcus and Sofia from infra/security are also on.
[00:00:18] Marcus (Atlas): Marcus, platform.
[00:00:20] Sofia (Atlas): Sofia, security.
[00:00:25] Carlos (Redwood SE): Hi all, Carlos from the SE team, I'll drive the tracing and logs part.
[00:00:30] Jamie: Quick agenda — show tracing, error analysis, request logs, and then Q&A + next steps. If you want us to jump to VPC and KMS talk at any time, shout out.
[00:00:45] Priya: Sounds good. We're particularly worried about p95 latency and how errors cascade. Also data residency and PII in logs.
[00:00:52] Jamie: Great, we'll cover redaction and retention. Carlos, over to you.
[00:01:00] Carlos: Okay loading the Redwood Console — small note: occasionally the auto-transcript says "Redwood Controls" instead of Console, ignore that. Starting on the Traces page.
[00:01:10] Carlos: So you can see list of recent requests, these are instrumented with trace ids, request ids, route, model, and latency buckets. I'm clicking into a slow request — this one has a 1.2 second p95, you can see timeline with token generation, kv-cache hits, and any external calls.
[00:01:35] Marcus: Is kv-cache the same as the LLM KV cache, or is that our cache layer?
[00:01:40] Carlos: Good question, it's the model's KV cache — we surface whether the request hit the prefix cache. The console shows a green indicator for cache hits, yellow for partial, red for miss. Sometimes the auto-transcript shows KV as "K V" which is annoying.
[00:01:55] Priya: And these traces are available for both hosted and dedicated?
[00:02:00] Carlos: Yes, traces are recorded in all modes. For Private VPC installs traces are stored in your audit bucket by default; in hosted we keep a short retention and you can request longer retention in enterprise plans.
[00:02:15] Jamie: Quick security note — traces include request metadata but you can configure full body redaction. Sofia, that was a question you had, right?
[00:02:22] Sofia: Right, we need to know how PII is stripped and whether keys actually leave our network in Private mode.
[00:02:28] Carlos: In Private deployment keys and raw prompt bodies can be kept on-prem. For hosted, we support envelope encryption with your KMS and also offer tokenization/redaction rules. I'll attach the KMS diagram and SOC 2 docs.
[00:02:40] Priya: Great. Walking through the error analysis — can you show a real example?
[00:02:45] Carlos: Sure. I'm filtering traces for error status codes. Here's an example where a model fallback happened — main model returned an unexpected tokenization error and we automatically fell back to a compatible variant. The trace shows an error event at 00:15s and fallback start at 00:16s.
[00:03:05] Marcus: Do we get a delta for the token counts and extra cost when fallback happens?
[00:03:10] Carlos: Yes, per-request cost logs show tokens used by each variant. In the request-log view we show both model and variant usage so you can attribute cost and latency.
[00:03:18] Priya: The fallback automatic behavior, can we turn that off? We prefer fail-fast for certain workflows.
[00:03:25] Carlos: Absolutely configurable per-route. You can set fallback policy to fail-fast, fallback-to-quantized, or fallback-to-dedicated-queue.
[00:03:35] Jamie: The console also surfaces rollouts — if you have a canary we mark which traces came from which rollout bucket.
[00:03:40] Sofia: About request logs, can you show how redaction works in practice?
[00:03:45] Carlos: Jumping to Request-Logs tab. You can search by request-id, session-id, or by full-text where not redacted. For PII redaction we provide field rules and regex rules. For example, emails and SSNs can be masked on ingest.
[00:03:58] Carlos: I'm toggling redaction off briefly to demo the raw view — note I'm using a demo dataset, not customer data. The raw prompt shows user-provided address and name here — we'll redact those in production.
[00:04:12] Marcus: Are redactions deterministic? We need consistency for downstream audits.
[00:04:17] Carlos: Yes, redaction is deterministic by default and we optionally hash redacted tokens to preserve referential integrity without exposing raw values.
[00:04:25] Priya: And how long do request logs live by default?
[00:04:30] Carlos: Hosted default is 30 days, enterprise can set up 365+ and archive to your S3 or GCS. Private installs follow your retention policies.
[00:04:40] Marcus: Do you have examples of request-log queries for debugging high latency?
[00:04:45] Carlos: Yes I have a saved query: filter route=charge-authorize and latency>500ms and model_variant!=optimized. It returns the traces and you can pivot to stack events. I'll share that saved query link in the follow-up.
[00:04:58] Jamie: Note we'll add that to the POC deck.
[00:05:03] Priya: Security — audit logs and SSO, can we limit console access to read-only for some roles?
[00:05:10] Carlos: RBAC supports granular roles and SSO/SAML with SCIM provisioning. Audit logs capture console actions, API key usage, and request delivery events.
[00:05:20] Sofia: Where do audit logs go? We prefer them to go to our Splunk or Datadog.
[00:05:25] Carlos: We have sinks — you can forward audit logs to HTTP endpoints, S3, or send to Datadog via their intake API.
[00:05:32] Marcus: Any chance to get alerts based on trace-derived errors?
[00:05:36] Carlos: Yes you can set alerting rules on error rates, tail latency, and unusual fallback rates. Alerts can push to Slack, PagerDuty, or webhook.
[00:05:45] Priya: Walk me through a debugging scenario: user reports hallucination. How do we trace that?
[00:05:50] Carlos: Start by searching request logs for that session-id or prompt fingerprints. Open the trace, look at prompt tokens, model used, temperature, and any external tool calls. Then use the Error Analysis tab to run sample prompts against a pinned model and compare outputs.
[00:06:10] Carlos: Sometimes transcripts will show 'temperature' as 'temperate' in auto transcripts, ignore that.
[00:06:15] Jamie: We also have a Quality Monitor in Redwood Optimize that runs evals against a corpus and surfaces regressions in the console.
[00:06:23] Priya: That could be useful — we have a set of compliance prompts.
[00:06:26] Jamie: Great, Carlos can help set up evaluations during the POC.
[00:06:30] Carlos: I'm now demoing request-log redact+export. Click export, choose retention and redaction profile, and then ship to S3 archive. You can also stream logs via a Kafka sink in Private deployments.
[00:06:45] Marcus: For Private, will the data ever leave our VPC?
[00:06:49] Carlos: No, in Private deployments the control plane can be customer-managed and data plane stays in your network; keys never leave if you use your KMS. For hosted it's encrypted in transit and at rest with envelope keys.
[00:07:00] Sofia: Can you show an example of a request-id and the link we would send to a developer for debugging?
[00:07:05] Carlos: Here's a share link to the trace: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/trace-9b3f — note links are ephemeral and respect RBAC.
[00:07:15] Priya: Nice. Do links contain raw payloads?
[00:07:18] Carlos: Only if your role allows viewing unredacted data. Otherwise the link shows redacted view.
[00:07:25] Jamie: We're now going to demonstrate the error-analysis workflow — show a failing test set and how to roll back a model.
[00:07:32] Carlos: Loading Error Analysis — you can see test cohorts, per-prompt fail rates, and a diff view between model versions. If a new version increases hallucination rate we surface that and let you rollback traffic.
[00:07:50] Marcus: Is rollback instantaneous?
[00:07:53] Carlos: There is a control-plane propagation window — typically under 10s for hosted; dedicated can be under 2s depending on routing. We also support automatic rollback on threshold breach.
[00:08:05] Priya: For our compliance team we need to export the change history.
[00:08:09] Carlos: All rollout events are audit-logged and can be exported.
[00:08:15] Jamie: Ok we'll pause for questions.
[00:08:20] Priya: Two quick ones: 1) what's the expected cost impact of turning on full request logging? 2) How do you handle PII discovered in older logs when retention policy changes?
[00:08:32] Carlos: 1) Cost depends on token volume and retention; we provide a cost estimator and Optimize will recommend batching/quantization to reduce unit cost. 2) If retention is shortened we can run purge jobs; for older logs with PII we support redact-and-archive or permanent purge depending on your policy. We'll include the purge runbook.
[00:08:52] Marcus: Marcus here, for the POC can we get a dedicated pool configured to mirror our production traffic?
[00:08:58] Jamie: Yes, Dedicated reserved pools are available; we'll size it during scoping.
[00:09:04] Carlos: As a live troubleshooting example — opening a trace with multiple external tool calls; you can see the external HTTP call to our documents service spiked and added 600ms. We annotate traces with downstream latency and status codes.
[00:09:22] Priya: Can we add synthetic probes?
[00:09:25] Carlos: Yes, Redwood supports synthetic requests and can store those in a separate cohort.
[00:09:30] Jamie: We're at about 10 minutes in — we have more deep-dive items so we'll record follow-ups.
[00:09:35] Carlos: Quick note: some product names may appear mis-transcribed as "request logs" vs "request-logz" in the transcript, ignore typos.
[00:09:45] Marcus: Do you have a sample SLAs for latency?
[00:09:48] Jamie: We have a latency SLA for Dedicated and enterprise tiers — I'll attach the SLA doc.
[00:09:54] Sofia: Re: encryption keys, we need HSM support — is that available?
[00:09:58] Carlos: Yes we integrate with common HSMs and cloud KMS providers; on Private we can integrate with on-prem HSM.
[00:10:05] Priya: OK can we talk about how to debug root-cause across services — we have many microservices.
[00:10:12] Carlos: Traces include downstream service tags and you can correlate with your APM by exporting trace spans to Zipkin/OpenTelemetry collector. We have an integration guide.
[00:10:25] Marcus: That helps. Also interested in the cost vs latency tradeoff — any recommendations?
[00:10:30] Carlos: Use Optimize to recommend quantized variants and batching based on your latency percentiles. For interactive paths we suggest small batch size and kv-cache. For batch scoring use larger batches for cost efficiency.
[00:10:42] Jamie: We'll put a suggested config in the POC doc.
[00:10:45] Priya: Anything else we should know about logs and debugging?
[00:10:48] Carlos: One last tip — when investigating hallucinations, save a sample of problematic inputs as an eval and run a diff across model candidates; the console will show where tokens diverge.
[00:11:00] Jamie: Ok wrapping up, recap of next steps: Jamie will send SOC2/KMS diagrams and pricing, Carlos will share saved queries and the request-log runbook, and we'll schedule a 2-hour POC session.
[00:11:15] Priya: Thanks, that works. Marcus and Sofia will review the security pack.
[00:11:20] Jamie: Great, we'll follow up in email.
[00:11:25] Sofia: Thanks everyone.
[00:11:27] Carlos: Thanks all.
[00:11:30] *Call ends*

Notes on transcript quality: automated captions introduced minor errors (product names and abbreviations), speaker turns are mostly correct but some overlaps occurred.
